sources.name: Financial Statements of the Government of New Zealand for the year ended 30 June 2025
sources.assumptions: Treasury's FY2025 financial statements report Gross companies tax, Refunds, and NRWT as a combined 'corporate tax' total, and RWT on interest/dividends as a separate 'other direct income tax' line - they don't itemise a Maori authority tax figure the way this dataset's plan-rate object still assumes (that rate is unused against this dataset). FY2025 actual figures: gross companies tax $17,727m, refunds $964m, NRWT $733m, RWT on interest $3,567m, RWT on dividends $940m - each divided by its component's rate (28%/15%/33%) to get the back-derived taxable base above. RWT on dividends fell sharply from FY2024's $2,521m - a genuine year-on-year change, not a data error.

sources.name: IRD - Non-resident withholding tax (NRWT) rates
sources.assumptions: NRWT is actually 0%/15%/30%, plus DTA-specific rates, depending on shareholder and income type. The flat 15% used to back-derive the NRWT base above is a simplification, not the headline rate.

sources.name: IRD - Resident withholding tax (RWT) rates
sources.assumptions: RWT on interest is tiered 10.5%/17.5%/28%/33%/39% by the recipient's elected rate; only RWT on dividends is genuinely flat at 33%. The flat 33% used to back-derive the RWT base above is a simplification.

sources.name: Green Party 2026 tax policy
sources.assumptions: Proposes a 33% corporate tax rate for companies with >$30M turnover (~0.7% of businesses), estimated to raise ~$5.9bn over 4 years (~$1.475bn/year). 'corpLarge' models this as a second corporate-tax component alongside the flat 'corp' one, applied identically to both years since the policy isn't tied to a specific historical year.

sources.name: Deloitte NZ - Election tax policies
sources.assumptions: Independently estimates the same large-company rate rise at $1.37-1.57bn/year, bracketing the Green Party's own figure. corpLarge's taxable-income base (~$29.5bn) is back-derived as annual_revenue / (0.33-0.28) from these estimates - no IRD/Stats NZ company-tax-by-turnover-band split exists publicly to source it independently. That $29.5bn is subtracted out of 'corp's Gross Corporate figure below, so 'corp' represents only the <=$30M-turnover cohort and the two components sum back to the real FY total - refunds aren't split by company size (no data exists to do so), so they stay wholly under 'corp'.
